name: Malachi

objectives.text: Identify Malachi as the last book of the Old Testament in the order of the English Bible
Recall that in Malachi God calls himself a Father and Master who deserves honor from his people
Retell how God told the people they were robbing him by holding back their tithes and offerings
Recall that God promised to send the prophet Elijah before the great day of the Lord
Summarize the main complaints God brings against the people and the questions they ask in reply
Explain how the Gospels identify John the Baptist as the messenger God promised to send ahead of the Lord
Compare the blemished sacrifices and careless attitude of the priests with the honoring worship God required
Describe the book of remembrance and what it shows about God's care for those who fear him
Explain the principle behind God's command about tithes and offerings and the promise attached to it
Place Malachi in its post-exilic setting by relating its concerns to the problems Nehemiah confronted
Analyze the disputation pattern of statement, objection, and reply that structures the book
Explain the images of the refiner's fire and fuller's soap and what they teach about the Lord's coming to purify his people
Interpret the statement I have loved Jacob but Esau I have hated in light of its covenant context and Paul's use of it
Connect the promise of the sun of righteousness rising with healing to the coming of Jesus Christ
Explain Malachi's teaching on intermarriage with idolaters and on divorce as faithlessness to the covenant
Analyze the covenant with Levi and how the priests failed in their calling to teach true instruction
Explain how Malachi's promise that God's name will be great among the nations anticipates worship of God by the Gentiles
Construct a profile of the spiritual complacency of the post-exilic community using evidence from the text
Explain how Malachi presents the day of the Lord as both judgment on the wicked and deliverance for the righteous
Evaluate the claim that the promised Elijah was fulfilled in John the Baptist using Jesus' own words
Defend the Reformed doctrine of God's immutability from Malachi's declaration I the Lord do not change
Synthesize how Malachi's closing call to remember the law of Moses and await Elijah links the Old Testament canon to the opening of the New Testament

changes: Kept all sixteen original competencies with rewording: changed tithes from personal application to explaining the principle, and reframed the 400 years of silence as the canonical link between Malachi and the Gospels. Added objectives on the book of remembrance, the post-exilic setting with Nehemiah, the refiner's fire, the covenant with Levi, God's name among the nations, and the day of the Lord, which are major sections of the book that were missing. Anchored each objective to specific verses and added New Testament fulfillment texts and fitting Westminster references.
